The '''2013–14 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team''' represented [[Duke University]] during the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by thirty-fourth year and [[List of coaches in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] head coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]]. They played its home games at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the season 26–9, 13–5 in ACC play to finish in a tie for third place. They advanced to the championship game of the [[2014 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] where they lost to Virginia. They received an at-large bid to the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the second round to Mercer.

==Previous season==
In November, The Blue Devils won the [[Battle 4 Atlantis]] tournament in the Bahamas, defeating Louisville in the championship game. The Blue Devils posted four victories against top 5 opponents (at the time of the game) and were undefeated (16-0) at home. Completing the season with 30 wins (and 6 losses; 14–4 in ACC play), Duke finished in second place in the ACC regular season standings. Duke was ranked in the top 10 of the AP poll all season long, including five weeks at #1. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2013 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] to Maryland and subsequently received a two seed in the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]]. They defeated Albany in the Round of 64, #22 Creighton in the Round of 32, and #9 Michigan State in the Sweet Sixteen to reach the Elite Eight. Duke lost to #1 overall seed and eventual NCAA champion Louisville in the Elite Eight in Indianapolis who reversed the game result from the meeting earlier in the season.

==Schedule==
In Duke's [[2013–14 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2013–14 ACC season]] opening 79–77 loss against [[2013–14 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]], Krzyzewski endured his 1st loss to one of his former assistant coaches after 18 wins.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=209358757|title=Notes: Notre Dame 79, Duke 77|access-date=2014-01-05|date=2014-01-04|work=GoDuke.com}}</ref> With the loss, Duke fell from the top 10 in the [[AP Poll]] for the first time in 122 weeks of the poll (since November 26, 2007).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/92094/new-poll-ends-one-crazy-duke-streak?ex_cid=espnapi_public|title=New AP poll ends one crazy Duke streak|access-date=2014-01-07|date=2014-01-06|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Brennan, Eamonn}}</ref> On January 25, Duke defeated [[2013–14 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] to achieve Krzyzewski's 900th win at Duke.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400502810|title=Mike Krzyzewski wins 900th game as Duke coach|access-date=2014-01-27|date=2014-01-25|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> The Blue Devils were upset by [[2013-14 Mercer Bears men's basketball team|Mercer]], 78–71 in the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]'s 2nd round, to conclude their season.
